episode_text: The AI evaluated several custom UI and optimization components for a Next.js project to determine their necessity. It concluded that custom image loaders and empty utilities were redundant or overly complex compared to Next.js built-in features, and decided to remove them while retaining valuable UX components like the loading skeleton. The codebase was refactored to use native framework capabilities instead of custom wrappers. | Custom intersection observer image loader: Replaced with Next.js Image component using built-in lazy loading and priority props | Empty middleware file: Temporarily removed to eliminate confusion and maintenance overhead | Manual preloading via React refs: Migrated to Next.js priority attributes and native browser optimizations | Poor loading UX: Solved by retaining LoadingSkeleton with Tailwind animate-pulse for structured, accessible placeholders | Remove SmartImageLoader and OptimizedImage due to redundancy with Next.js native features | Keep LoadingSkeleton for improved perceived performance and user feedback | Delete the empty middleware.ts file until specific security or caching requirements emerge | Replace all custom image loading logic with the standard Next.js Image component | Avoid manual DOM manipulation for image preloading in favor of framework-optimized approaches | Framework-native optimization over custom abstraction layers | Skeleton screens over spinners for content-aware loading states | Usage-driven component lifecycle management

facts.content: The AI decided to remove SmartImageLoader and OptimizedImage components because they were redundant with Next.js native Image component features like built-in lazy loading and priority props.
The AI decided to retain LoadingSkeleton component with Tailwind animate-pulse for structured, accessible placeholders to improve perceived performance and user feedback.
The AI decided to delete the empty middleware.ts file to eliminate confusion and maintenance overhead until specific security or caching requirements emerge.
The AI prefers framework-native optimization over custom abstraction layers when refactoring Next.js projects.
The AI prefers skeleton screens over spinners for content-aware loading states to provide better user experience.
